checks.evidence: Action: Observe the loaded scene in motion, seek 0/30/120/17/73 and select each rendered body. Expected: One sun, three size/color-distinct planets and fixed 12/24/48-second circular phases. Observed: Gold sun, small tan Mercury, blue Earth and larger orange Jupiter render with curved perspective orbits. At t=30 native scene picks identify Mercury/Earth/Jupiter at their predicted 180/90/225-degree positions; t=17.25 displays 157.5/258.8/129.4 degrees. Visible positions change with time and repeat after reload, matching the inspected fixed-phase equations.

Action: Open and reload the original HTTP page and observe subsequent motion. Expected: Time starts at zero, 1x, playing, null selection and overview. Observed: Reload shows t=0.4 after ordinary load elapsed time, speed 1, Pause, no selection and overview; the fresh startup sample advances 5.2 to 8.3 over about 3.1 seconds with visible orbital motion.

Action: Pause at 30, wait 0.5 seconds, use selection/camera and resume. Expected: Frozen paused time/positions and continuous resumed motion. Observed: Paused time remains 30 with unchanged angles; native selections and camera orbit still work. At 2x the resumed sample advances 30.5 to 36.6 over 3.1038 seconds without a reset or jump.

Action: Set 0.25x, 2x and 4x while paused and playing, then measure visible-document playback away from endpoints. Expected: Preserved position on setting and proportional advance. Observed: Paused samples stay t=30. The measured deltas are 0.7 over 3.1025s at 0.25x, 6.1 over 3.1038s at 2x, and 12.4 over 3.1041s at 4x, all inside preregistered rounding/scheduling tolerance. Playing changes preserve playback and current orbital progression.

Action: Seek 0,30,120,17,73 and repeat 30/17/73 after state edits and reload with the same mobile viewport and camera framing. Expected: Immediate paused positions with stable phases. Observed: Each seek pauses at the requested time. Decoded 335x324 scene-pixel regions for 30,17,73 have zero differing color channels after reload. PNG encodings differed, but decoded scene pixels did not. All three bodies were visible after ordinary user zoom-out.

Action: Resume from 119 at 4x, wait 3.1 seconds and another 0.6 seconds, then seek 17 and resume. Expected: Stop exactly at 120 without wrap and resume from earlier time. Observed: Both endpoint reads are 120 with Resume; the earlier-time run advances to 19.9 with Pause.

Action: Inspect CDN-loaded WebGLRenderer, SphereGeometry, PerspectiveCamera and orbit geometry, then perform native drag and wheel actions. Expected: Actual Three.js 3D rendering with changed depth/occlusion/perspective. Observed: Lit spherical surfaces, changing orbit ellipses and sun/planet occlusions respond to camera movement. A fresh tracking restore returns the original perspective. Resource timing records the Three.js CDN request; cross-origin responseStatus=0 is not treated as a load failure.

Action: Capture paused t=30/2x/Mercury/tracking, edit every live field, capture while playing, round-trip and reload, and import extra angle data. Expected: Immutable saved fields, three derived angles and stable unique IDs. Observed: Snapshot A remains 30/2/mercury/tracking with angles 180/90/225 after edits. IDs and complete list text survive reload. Playing capture appends without resetting live state. Imported t=0 with angles=[999] displays 0/0/0, while fractional 17.25 derives 157.5/258.8/129.4.

Action: Select Mercury, Earth and Jupiter through the native canvas and labeled select while paused and playing. Expected: Shared selection and visible highlight. Observed: All six scene/list routes identify the intended planet; playing canvas picks at about 30.1 return the expected IDs and updated information. Selected bodies brighten, including paused selection. Locator offset input was inconclusive; calibrated native mouse input established the result.

Action: Select each body, observe playback/seek, and restore null-selection overview after tracking. Expected: Name, period and angle agree with rendered selection, and null restoration clears information/highlight. Observed: t=30 shows Mercury 12s/180 degrees, Earth 24s/90 degrees and Jupiter 48s/225 degrees at their actual picked positions. Playback angles advance; null restore shows No planet selected and removes selected-body brightening.

Action: Track Mercury during a measured playback interval, seek 17/73 and switch to Earth; inspect null-selection tracking. Expected: Centered synchronized target, preserved live state and disabled/rejected tracking without selection. Observed: Mercury remains at the rendered scene center across observed moving/seek positions; the 390x844 screenshots place the selected center approximately at scene-image (168,162), within the 10% tolerance. Switching to Earth centers/brightens Earth and updates information without changing paused t=73. Null-selection tracking is disabled.

Action: Return from tracking to default overview at desktop size with snapshots present. Expected: Full-system overview with preserved live fields. Observed: Time/speed/selection/playback are preserved, but the outer orbital path is visibly cut by both horizontal canvas boundaries rather than showing the full system. User zoom-out can fit it, but the overview action alone does not. The failure is framing, not permitted vertical page scrolling.

Action: Restore the captured 2x tracking snapshot after changing the slider to 0.25, and restore the imported 1.5x null overview after unrelated edits. Expected: All displayed/restored state agrees and playback pauses with standard camera framing. Observed: Time/selection/mode/pause and repeated camera framing restore, but the speed slider retains 0.25 (later 0.95/3.95) while the adjacent label reports the restored 2.00x or 1.50x. Source update() never synchronizes the speed input.

Action: Native camera drags and wheel zoom in overview/tracking while paused and playing. Expected: Operable camera in all four states without simulation reset. Observed: All four rendered views change orientation and scale; paused time remains 30, and playing time advances naturally with selection/mode preserved. Wheel delivery used the actual canvas wheel handler; pointer drag used native mouse input.

Action: Begin fast and cumulative 30-CSS-pixel/20-move drags on Mercury while Earth is selected, then exercise DOM controls. Expected: Drags do not become selection clicks or leak DOM interactions into camera movement. Observed: Both drags retain Earth and t=30 while moving the camera. Primary DOM actions change only their intended state; a valid import preserves the scene exactly after aligning the page scroll offset.

Action: Inspect live, snapshot and JSON feedback throughout restore and storage-failure sequences. Expected: Consistent understandable state. Observed: Labeled sections and validation messages are clear, but restored speed label disagrees with the slider and failed import saving reports success. These repeated feedback contradictions match qualitative anchor 2.

Action: Capture three, reject a fourth, delete the middle and capture again. Expected: Visible capacity warning, immutable existing entries, unchanged live state and append-only unique replacement. Observed: Capacity reached message appears with byte-equivalent exported list; middle deletion retains the first/third IDs and values, and a fresh distinct ID appends. Live time/selection/mode/playback remain unchanged.

Action: At both required sizes operate selection by typeahead plus Enter, buttons by Enter, ranges by arrows, textarea editing/import/export, and Tab/Shift+Tab traversal. Expected: Named visible-focus controls operate without trapping focus. Observed: Typeahead selects Mercury at both sizes; all primary button/range/snapshot/JSON actions produce corresponding state changes. Focus outlines are solid and visible; traversal leaves and returns to the frame. Home/ArrowDown-only select attempts were inconclusive, not counted as failures because ordinary typeahead worked.

Action: Inspect default overview, tracking and zoomed views at both sizes. Expected: Consistently readable scene and selection. Observed: Spherical bodies and selected brightening are readable, especially tracking, but default overview repeatedly clips outer orbital geometry and the smallest planet is visually weak. The recurring observation ambiguity matches anchor 2; user zoom-out improves it.

Action: Inspect typography, spacing and simulation/planet/snapshot/JSON panels at both sizes. Expected: Coherent legible hierarchy. Observed: Dark bordered cards, consistent text sizes and well-separated controls remain legible, including wrapped snapshot IDs and angles. This is clear ordinary execution, anchor 3.

Action: Exercise every primary control at measured 1440x900, including keyboard snapshot/JSON actions. Expected: Usable scene/controls without horizontal scrolling or panel occlusion. Observed: Document clientWidth and scrollWidth are both 1423. Controls remain reachable with permitted vertical scrolling, and the camera/selection scene is operable. Default full-system framing is separately failed under T4.

Action: Repeat full primary-control operation at measured 390x844. Expected: Usable scene and all controls without horizontal overflow. Observed: Client/scroll widths both equal 373; stacked panels remain reachable with vertical scrolling, and selection, camera modes, sliders, playback, snapshot and JSON operations work. This is embedded CSS-viewport proof, not physical touch-device testing.

Action: Inspect index.html and its references while serving output as HTTP root. Expected: Complete local assets without build or repository-root dependencies. Observed: All local implementation is in index.html; the sole external Three.js CDN dependency is allowed. No referenced local file is missing.

Action: Establish fresh console-error and asynchronous thrown-exception positive controls on the owned scratch origin, then enable Runtime and Network before artifact navigation and throughout native-control sequences at actual top-level 1440x900 and 390x844, including playback/seek/speed/selection/tracking/overview, camera input, snapshots, JSON, reload, malformed saved data and real quota-write failures. Expected: No artifact-caused console/page errors or failed required resources prevent intended operation. Observed: Both Runtime.consoleAPICalled and Runtime.exceptionThrown controls were captured. Artifact sequences produced no console-error calls, uncaught page exceptions or Network.loadingFailed events. index.html and required Three.js returned successful effective HTTP 200 responses (reload revalidation/cache included). The Three.js legacy-build deprecation warning and automatic favicon.ico 404 were nonblocking. Actual UI capture/restore/delete/export/import and reload paths ran; quota capture warned, while quota import still exhibited the historically failed saving-feedback defect without an uncaught error. D3 passes its diagnostic condition, not the separate historical mandatory failures.

Action: Export empty/populated lists, round-trip through labeled textarea/import/export, and compare state/order/IDs. Expected: Exact version-1 five-field schema and visible planet-ID mapping with no implicit live-state mutation. Observed: Empty export is version 1 with an empty array; populated exports contain only id/time/speed/selectedPlanet/viewMode and preserve order, case/spaces and typed values. Mercury/mercury, Earth/earth, Jupiter/jupiter mappings are visible. Paused and playing round-trips preserve live state apart from natural advance.

Action: Run 37 invalid classes and valid empty/three-entry/boundary/fractional/case-sensitive/spaced-ID/extra-key payloads while paused and playing. Expected: Atomic rejection with visible errors or list-only replacement, derived angles and camera preservation. Observed: Every invalid case, including mixed validity and overflow, shows an error and preserves the exact existing list/live fields. Valid 0/120 and 0.25/4 endpoints, 17.25/1.5, whitespace-only ID and extra keys succeed. Extra angles are ignored. Import camera comparison initially had a 47-image-pixel scroll offset; after aligning the observed header shift, all four body centers have zero shift.

Action: Reload after import/delete/capture; replace owned persisted data with malformed/version-invalid values; fill a unique quota key and perform UI writes. Expected: Persistent data or visible saving-unavailable feedback with usable in-memory controls. Observed: All normal mutations and derived text survive reload; invalid storage recovers visibly to an empty list. A real failed capture write warns correctly, but a larger valid import fails to change durable storage while replacing the warning with Snapshot list imported; live simulation unchanged. Memory-only import is incorrectly reported as success. Original raw storage was restored and quota key removed.
